data.one_liner: Embedded local database for Flutter with Rust/LMDB backend, Diesel-style queries, and reactive streams.
data.what_it_does: Provides a local database supporting both key-value records and relational tables mapped directly from your existing data models. Offers Diesel-style typed queries, joins, aggregates, transactions, offline-first sync, and reactive streams.
use_when: You want an offline-first Flutter application with complex querying requirements.
You prefer writing queries using Diesel-style DSL without using build_runner or complex code generation.
You need high-performance local storage backed by Rust and LMDB.
avoid_when: Your application targets platforms other than Android, iOS, web (key-value only), Windows, macOS, and Linux.
You need standard SQLite features through standard SQL strings rather than a Rust-powered query DSL.
strengths: No code generation or macros required for tables.
Supports reactive streams via watch queries.
Built on top of a fast Rust and LMDB engine with built-in offline-first sync support.
weaknesses: Tables require the db_dsl_lints analyzer plugin for typed field extensions to avoid manual string-based field paths.
Full database functionality (tables) is limited to non-web platforms; web only supports the key-value API.
data.setup_notes: Ships prebuilt with a build hook bundling native libraries for all target platforms. Enable the db_dsl_lints analyzer plugin in analysis_options.yaml for typed table fields.

alternatives.name: drift
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer a robust, type-safe SQLite database for Flutter with built-in SQL support and comprehensive migration tooling.

alternatives.name: sqflite
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you want a lightweight and widely-used standard SQLite plugin with direct SQL execution.

alternatives.name: shared_preferences
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you only need simple key-value persistence without tables or complex queries.
